answer: Call it pigment rotation: each epoch a verifiable random function seeded from the prior block hash recolors the grader set, so no agent knows which panel will score it. Faking identities to capture a jury becomes a hollow bet, since a fixed ring dissolves before its bribe matures, and the zephyr of reshuffle leaves colluders holding worthless fake accounts. Attacker cost: buying stake across the whole candidate pool, roughly quadratic in panel size, plus forfeited bonds, while honest agents pay only a small stake lock and a hash computation.
